mutants.reason: With PARA_SFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO=1 (a legal setting) the macro read enable is tied inactive, so the read register never loads and o_rd_data stays undefined/stale. Not visible only in the default array config.
The read-domain reset value of the empty flop becomes 0, so o_empty is 0 during and after hardware reset instead of 1.

The mutation swaps the array and macro branches. The macro model (read enable tied 0, active-low write enable, same one-cycle read latency, old data on same-edge read/write, no reset) behaves the same as the array, so the ports see no difference. Only the hierarchy changes.

The next read pointer is sign-extended with ones, so the occupancy in the read domain is wrong (off by 2xDEPTH). reg_empty and reg_empty_thr no longer follow the real occupancy and o_empty is never raised when the FIFO drains.

The acknowledge is inverted: it is 1 in RUN and 0 in ACK. The write FSM sees an ack before the read pointer is reset and the REL exit is wrong, so the software reset handshake and the o_sw_rst_busy timing are broken.
The block term is inverted: reads are blocked in normal RUN operation (o_empty stuck at 1) and unblocked in RST/ACK.

REL leaves for RUN when ack is 0 OR the read pointer is 0, instead of AND. The read pointer is already 0, so REL ends one cycle early while ack is still 1, and o_sw_rst_busy falls early and writes are released before the read side.
An accepted write adds 0 to the write pointer, so the pointer never advances. The occupancy stays 0, o_empty never falls, and words overwrite each other.

ACK leaves for RUN when request is 0 OR write pointer is 0, instead of AND. The read FSM can leave ACK while the request is still 1 (write pointer already 0 in HOLD) and loops RST/ACK, so the ack pattern, the o_sw_rst_busy timing and the read release timing change.
The busy flop is inverted: o_sw_rst_busy is 1 in RUN and 0 during the reset sequence.
The reset condition of the read flag flops is inverted. The flags are held at reset values (o_empty 1, o_empty_thr 1, ack/retiming flops 0) during normal operation, so o_empty never falls.
The condition is logically inverted, so the array and macro branches are swapped. The macro model and the array are port-equivalent, so no stimulus shows a difference.
The write pointer reset condition is inverted, so the pointer is held at 0 in normal operation. Writes never advance it, o_empty never falls, and data is lost.
The write-domain reset value of the full flop becomes 1, so o_full is 1 during and just after hardware reset instead of 0.
The request flop is set when the next state is not REQ (plus PTR/HOLD), so request is 1 in RUN and the read side is blocked or the read FSM is driven into reset without any software reset.

The read pointer wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, which never matches. For power-of-2 depths the pointer wraps by overflow anyway, but for other legal depths (5, 12) the pointer runs past 2xDEPTH-1 and occupancy and address are wrong.

The extended read pointer is filled with ones, so the wrap compare never matches. For power-of-2 depths the 4-bit increment wraps by itself, but for non-power-of-2 depths the read pointer does not wrap at 2xDEPTH and data and flags are wrong.
The ACK exit requires write pointer != 0 instead of == 0. The read FSM never leaves ACK after a software reset (the pointer is 0), so reads stay blocked.
With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=0 the read side uses the retimed (one-cycle-late) write pointer, so o_empty falls one read edge later than the direct-path requirement and the first-read latency grows.

The write pointer wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, which never matches. For power-of-2 depths the pointer wraps by overflow, but for other legal depths (5, 12) the pointer does not wrap correctly and full/occupancy and address are wrong.
With RETIME=0 the write FSM sees the ack through the retiming flop, one cycle late. The handshake and o_sw_rst_busy duration change.

The memory read address subtraction is inverted. For power-of-2 depths the low address bits are the same either way, but for other legal depths (5, 12) the read address is out of range or wrong, so o_rd_data shows the wrong word.
The memory stores when i_wr_en is 0 and ignores accepted writes, so accepted words are never stored and o_rd_data returns wrong data.
REQ proceeds when the ack is 0 instead of 1. The write FSM continues before the read side has reset its pointer and acknowledged, so the handshake and sequence timing and the final state are wrong.

The request flop resets to 1. If the read side is released first or at the same edge it sees request 1, so the read FSM enters RST/ACK, reads are blocked and no underflow pulse is raised. A write at the first edge can leave the read side stuck in ACK.
The write pointer is reset to 0 in every state except PTR, so an accepted write in RUN never advances the pointer.
An accepted read adds 0 to the read pointer, so the pointer never advances. The same word is returned again and o_empty/o_full do not follow the reads.

The reset value of the request retiming flop becomes 1. It is unused with PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=0, but with RETIME=1 (a legal setting) the read side sees a request after reset release and enters RST/ACK, so reads are blocked and flag timing changes.
The read pointer is reset to 0 in every state except RST, so an accepted read in RUN never advances the pointer.
With RETIME=0 the read side uses the retimed request, one cycle late. The read block and the FSM start one cycle later, so a read can be accepted in the cycle after the request.
With RETIME=0 the write side uses the retimed read pointer, so o_full falls one write edge later than the direct-path requirement.

The reset condition of the acknowledge flop is inverted, so the ack is held at 0 during operation. The write FSM waits in REQ forever and o_sw_rst_busy and o_full stay 1 after a software reset request.
The reset condition of the busy and request flops is inverted, so both are held at 0 in operation. o_sw_rst_busy never rises and the request never reaches the read side.
The extended full threshold is filled with ones, so the compare is never true and o_full_thr stays 0 even at or above i_full_thr.
While writes are blocked o_full_thr shows (i_full_thr != 0) instead of (i_full_thr == 0), the opposite of the empty-FIFO value.
The reset value of the empty-threshold flop becomes 0, so o_empty_thr is 0 during and after hardware reset instead of 1.
